title: Dialysis Water Source Crisis — Inpatient Urgency

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anita Shah
transcript.text: Anita Shah. Beyond the nine outpatients I have 24 inpatients on dialysis. Twenty-one are on intermittent hemodialysis using the portable RO units, which draw from the same affected supply; three are on continuous renal replacement in ICU 3 South using bagged sterile fluids, which are fine. Two inpatients have potassium above 6.0 this morning and cannot wait. I need a safe water source or a place to take them.

transcript.speaker: AOC
transcript.text: Dr. Shah, thank you. I’m on it. We’re activating the HCC now. The Liaison Officer will contact the regional healthcare coalition for a partner facility with dialysis capacity outside the advisory area. We’ll assess if we can use bottled sterile water prepared by Pharmacy for the two high-potassium patients. Is the lab able to confirm hyperkalemia on the most recent labs?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anita Shah
transcript.text: Yes, lab confirmed 6.2 and 6.4. Both are on the verge of arrhythmia. We need to treat within the hour. The portable RO units are down and we can’t use the main loop. I’m not waiting.

transcript.speaker: AOC
transcript.text: Understood. I’m authorizing Pharmacy to prepare 500mL sterile water bottles for immediate use under the EHR Downtime Procedures Annex, Section 5.3 — emergency fluid sourcing. You’ll have three bottles per patient. I’ll alert the CMO and have the HCC issue a priority alert to the coalition. You have 45 minutes to initiate treatment.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anita Shah
transcript.text: Roger that. We’re starting now. I’ll keep you posted.
